classes.title: Monthly per-agent commission cap applied by a ledger trigger outside COMMISSION_PKG
classes.causing_condition: BEFORE INSERT trigger TRG_LEDGER_MONTHLY_CAP reduces commission_amt so an agent's COMMISSION rows for a period never exceed 2500.00; COMMISSION_PKG computes the uncapped amount and has no reference to the cap

classes.title: Tier rate change takes effect one day late (strict greater-than on change_date)
classes.causing_condition: RESOLVE_TIER_RATE selects rows with p_as_of > change_date, so a policy issued on the change date is paid the previous rate

classes.title: Premium tier boundary drifted between COMMISSION_PKG and DW_ETL_PKG
classes.causing_condition: OLTP PREMIUM_TIER puts annual_premium = 50000 in T2 (< 50000 is T1); the ETL uses BETWEEN 0 AND 50000 for T1, so the seeded 50000.00 policy is T2 in the ledger and T1 in fact_commission

classes.title: Early-lapse chargeback: code reverses 100% inside 12 months, spec grades 100%/50%
classes.causing_condition: LAPSE_POLICY books a CHARGEBACK of the full commission paid whenever MONTHS_BETWEEN(lapse, issue) < 12; spec CP-114 section 6.1 charges back 100% for months 1-6 and 50% for months 7-12

classes.title: Product and commission specification exists only as an image-only scan
classes.causing_condition: spec/cp114-commission-spec-scan.pdf is three skewed, noisy JPEG page images with no text layer (no fonts, pdftotext empty); rules must be read with a vision model
classes.surfaces_in: spec ingestion: the chargeback rule disagreeing with code is only stated here

removed_hints.original_text:
the database-centric *before state* that stored-procedure modernization demos
extract from.

business rules are in `COMMISSION_PKG`; there is deliberately no application
  tier duplicating them.

This is a local, disposable fixture: loopback-only port bindings, per-namespace
Compose projects and volumes, and fixed well-known fixture credentials. It is
intentionally **not** deployed to Helm/EKS or any shared environment. A real
modernization target must add authentication, authorization, tenant scoping,
and secret management at the service edge — none of which exist in the legacy
database-centric design, which is part of the point.
